seo_description: An interactive visualization of Cohen's d effect size: the overlap of two distributions, Cohen's U3, the probability of superiority, percentage of overlap, and the number needed to treat.
title: Interpreting Cohen's d Effect Size
subtitle: An Interactive Visualization
intro_p1: The Cohen's d effect size is immensely popular in psychology. However, its interpretation is not straightforward and researchers often use general guidelines, such as small (0.2), medium (0.5) and large (0.8) when interpreting an effect. Moreover, in many cases it is questionable whether the standardized mean difference is more interpretable than the unstandardized mean difference.
intro_p2: In order to aid the interpretation of Cohen's d, this visualization offers these different representations of Cohen's d: visual overlap, Cohen's U3, the probability of superiority, percentage of overlap, and the number needed to treat. It also lets you change the standard deviation and displays the unstandardized difference.

cl_sentence: With a Cohen's d of {d}, {u3} of the "{g1}" group will be above the mean of the "{g0}" group (Cohen's U3), {ovl} of the two groups will overlap, and there is a {cles} chance that a person picked at random from the "{g1}" group will have a higher score than a person picked at random from the "{g0}" group (probability of superiority). Moreover, in order to have one more favorable outcome in the "{g1}" group compared to the "{g0}" group, we need to treat {nnt} people on average. This means that if there are 100 people in each group, and we assume that {cer} people have favorable outcomes in the "{g0}" group, then {cer} + {nntPerc} people in the "{g1}" group will have favorable outcomes.1
cl_footnote: <sup>1</sup>The values are averages, and it is assumed that {cer} (CER) of the "{g0}" group have "favorable outcomes," i.e., their outcomes are below some cut-off. Change this using the Settings button above the slider. Go to the formula section for more information.
faq_help_q: How do I use this visualization?
faq_help_a1: Use the slider to change Cohen's d, or open the settings to change the parameters. The inputs can also be controlled with the keyboard arrows.
faq_help_a2: From the settings you can change the means, standard deviation, and the control group event rate (CER); the axis and distribution labels; and the slider's maximum and step size. Settings can be saved in your browser's localStorage so they persist across visits.
faq_help_a3: You can pan the x-axis by clicking and dragging the visualization. Double-click the visualization to recenter and rescale it.
